steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Place asparagus into a mixing bowl, drizzle with olive oil, and toss to coat.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and garlic; season to taste with salt and pepper if using. Arrange asparagus in a single layer in a baking dish or on a rimmed baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until just tender, 12 to 15 minutes depending on thickness. Sprinkle with lemon juice just before serving, and serve immediately for the best texture.

raw_recipe.headline: Oven-Roasted Asparagus
raw_recipe.description: Tender roasted asparagus, seasoned with minced garlic, Parmesan cheese, and lemon juice. Pairs perfectly with roast leg of lamb or grilled fish.

video.description: Have a healthy and delicious snack that you can cook using these three different techniques. In this video, Nicole shows you how to cook asparagus using an air fryer, an oven, and a grill. To cook them in an air fryer, toss the asparagus in olive oil before adding pink salt, peppercorns, garlic powder, crushed red pepper, and parmesan cheese. They will be cooked for around seven minutes before being crispy and ready to eat. To roast in the oven, toss them in olive oil before adding salt, pepper, garlic, and parmesan cheese. Bake them for around 15 minutes. Finally, grilling asparagus simply requires tossing them in olive oil and adding salt and pepper. After turning them on the grill for around 5 minutes, this healthy side dish and snack is ready to go!

review.reviewBody: I make this all the time, and it's unbelievably good! I use this recipe exactly, except I've never tried it with garlic. I'm going to try it next time! Also, instead of tossing the asparagus with the parmesan, I toss with all the other ingredients and lay in a single layer, then sprinkle the parmesan all over the top. I bake mine at 350 degrees for 10-12 minutes, depending on the thickness of the asparagus. Oh, and a hint: if you line the baking sheet with aluminum foil, there's hardly any clean up!
Nice recipe, however I prefer my asparagus to be a little crisper. 12 minutes was too long for the thick stalks I had... 8 minutes would be about right at 425.

Be sure to follow the footnote tip to remove tough part of stem by snapping the asparagus in two. The fresher it is, the better this works, so I do this as soon as I get home from the store (also makes weeknight cooking quicker & easier when I am ready to make). I also like to line the baking sheet with aluminum foil for easy clean up. Instead of tossing with olive oil I spray with cooking spray after the asparagus is spread in an even layer on the sheet. I promise it tastes just as good. Then I sprinkle with coarse salt & fine pepper (sprinkle from up high to more evenly distribute the seasonings).
I used fresh long green beans instead of asparagus, because the asparagus was out of season. delicious!

Used EVOO, salt and pepper, garlic powder and parmesan. Tossed asparagus in olive oil, generously sprinkled my spices, baked it and it was HEAVENLY. My dad who hates "rabbit food" (vegetables) raved about it and everyone wished I made more. Keep a careful eye on them, mine only took 6-8 minutes at that hot of an oven. I lowered the temp to 350 and they browned a little slower - less chance of a quick burn.
Loved it! Simple good dish. I did add some Italian seasoning to make the flavor mesh better with our Italian meal, but that is the only change I made!

I made this along with another asparagus dish (asparagus with junk from this site) because I wasn't sure which way our guests would like the asparagus. I followed the recipe except I cut down the sea salt in half, I think if you use regular table salt you can use as much as stated in the original recipe but sea salt gives it a way better flavor. I also only had parmesan & Romano cheese blend in fridge. I cleaned the asparagus drizzled with olive oil in a bowl then added the rest of the ingredients after I put the asparagus onto a cookie sheet lined with tin foil. I rolled the asparagus in salt, pepper and garlic then sprinkled the parm and roasted in oven at 325 for about 18 min. This was a huge hit, every spear was devoured. Thank You for sharing
Love this. I don't use lemon juice but I do add frozen broccoli & cauliflower and I wait to put the parmesan cheese on until the last couple minutes. I can eat a cookie sheet of veggies all by myself

I am blown away by this. I had no idea it would turn out this good. Even my husband said it was really, really good, and he's a meat-and-potatoes kind of guy. I halved the salt and still think it's salty, so maybe next time I'll use 1/4 teaspoon, but that's my only complaint. I did sprinkle some sliced almonds over the asparagus after it was spread out on the baking sheet, and that was a nice touch.

I have been making asparagus like this for a long time now. It's the only way I prepare it. My husband never had asparagus until I introduced it to him this way and he loves it. I use granulated garlic in lieu of fresh because the fresh tends to burn and get bitter. I also only use a couple of healthy pinches of Diamond Krystal Kosher salt. Sea salt and table salt can be very "salty". DK is all I use. Just a kitchen hack (tip) that I use when making this and other vegetables that require a coating of oil is placing the vegetables in a gallon zip lock bag and mix it all together that way. It saves on dishes!

Thank you for creating an asparagus recipe that accommodates the super-thin stalks that seem to be the only ones I can find these days. I baked them for 12 minutes with garlic, salt, pepper, and olive oil, adding lemon juice at the end. They were delicious!
YUMMY!! Everyone loves it! Followed recipe as written
Absolutely amazing!! Super easy and delicious!!
Delicious! My husband said it was the best asparagus he’s ever eaten. It is a keeper

I made this for Easter dinner and everyone loved them. I didn't have fresh garlic so I used garlic salt in place of the salt. I only used 2 Tbsp of olive oil for a 28 oz package of asparagus which was plenty. I also cooked it at 400 for 12 minutes since they were thin.
This is easy and delicious.
Great tasting.
First time adding garlic and that definitely made this the best roasted asparagus!
Mine turned out dried out and stringy. The seasoning was a saving grace. It might have been the stalks as the bottoms were white but I trimmed off that part. Will try again with better asparagus.

Delicious. I followed the recipe exactly. I skipped the bowl and mixed everything right on the sheet pan for easier clean up. I used Costco chopped jarred garlic because when it's roasted it gets sweet. My new go-to asparagus dish.
